newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jury tells ABC to pay Food Lion $5.5 million.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jury tells ABC to pay Food Lion $5.5 million.

text.p: A federal jury on Wednesday awarded Food Lion Inc. $5.5 million in connection with the ABC Televison "PrimeTime Live" report on its food handling.

After more than five days of deliberations, the panel of six men and six women returned a decision ordering ABC-TV to pay $4 million and American Broadcasting Co. to pay $1.5 million in punitive damages. ABC-TV and its parent, American Broadcasting Companies, are units of Walt Disney Co..

The jury also ordered two high-ranking "PrimeTime Live" producers to pay damages to Food Lion for the 1992 story that examined Food Lion's meat handling practices. ABC Executive producer Richard Kaplan, who approved the undercover story, was told to pay $35,000 in punitive damages and senior producer Ira Rosen was ordered to pay $10,750.
Neither of the two ABC journalists who worked undercover for Food Lion preparing the story with hidden cameras was ordered to pay punitive damages.

The jury returned its verdict in the case after more than 29 hours of deliberations that began last week. Food Lion sued ABC and four of its producers for a 1992 hidden-camera investigation that claimed the supermarket chain sold old meat and fish and its food-handling practices were unsafe.

The grocery chain did not challenge the truth of the report, but filed a lawsuit accusing ABC of fraud by having two journalists break the law to to get jobs with Food Lion. Last month, the same jury awarded Food Lion $1,400 in actual damages.
